flashcards.back: Speedup = 1 / ((1 - F) + F/S). The unaffected fraction (1 - F) caps total speedup. Even infinite S gives at most 1/(1 - F).
CPU time = Instruction Count × CPI × Clock Cycle Time.
P = ½ × C × V² × f × α. Voltage has the dominant effect (squared); activity factor α is what clock gating attacks.
It's independent of the reference machine and resists outliers — arithmetic mean is biased by the largest speedups.
Availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR). 'Five nines' = 99.999% = ~5 minutes downtime per year.
Reducing V cuts dynamic power as V², and lower V allows lower f, giving roughly V³ effective scaling. Halving V cuts power ~8×.
The fraction of a chip that must be powered down at any moment because thermal/power budget can't support all transistors switching. Drove the multicore + accelerator era.
Yield = (1 + (defects × area) / N)^(-N). Doubling die area more than doubles defects per die — yield drops exponentially.
AMAT = Hit_time + Miss_rate × Miss_penalty. Multi-level: AMAT = Hit_L1 + MR_L1 × (Hit_L2 + MR_L2 × Penalty_L2)...
Compulsory (first reference), Capacity (working set > cache), Conflict (set associativity insufficient). 4th C: Coherence (multicore).
Through: every write to cache + memory (simple, high BW). Back: cache only, write to memory on eviction (low BW, dirty bit). L1/L2 = back, almost always.
Translation Lookaside Buffer — small cache (32-1024 entries) of virtual-to-physical page translations. Multi-level on modern chips. Huge pages reduce pressure.
TLB miss: hardware page walk, ~tens of cycles. Page fault: page not in memory at all, OS traps, swaps from disk, ~ms.
Adds root/non-root mode + VMCS so hypervisor can configure guest traps. EPT/NPT does 2-level address translation in hardware. Foundation of modern cloud.
Hardware unit that detects sequential accesses with constant stride (array traversal) and prefetches N blocks ahead. Modern CPUs run 6-8 streams at once.
Re-Reference Interval Prediction — 2-bit per-line counter for predicted re-reference distance. Beats LRU on scan-resistant workloads. Modern Intel/AMD L3.
Tree-based approximation: N-1 bits per N-way set. Within 2-3% of true LRU at fraction of the storage. Used in nearly all L2/L3.
RAW: read after write (true dependence — can't remove). WAR/WAW: name dependences, eliminated by register renaming. Modern OoO does this implicitly.
Reservation stations (operand wait), Common Data Bus (broadcast results), Register status table (renaming map). 1967 IBM 360/91. Foundation of all OoO.
Holds instructions in program order from issue to commit. Out-of-order execute, in-order commit. Enables precise exceptions and speculation. M1 has 600+ entries.
1-bit → 2-bit (bimodal) → correlating (m,n) → tournament → TAGE/perceptron. Modern hits 97-99%. At 95% with 20-stage pipeline, mispredict = 80 instructions of wasted work.
SMT: 2 threads share one core's FUs/ROB → ~30% throughput gain for ~5% area (Intel HT, AMD SMT). Apple M-series skips SMT for single-thread perf.
With perfect prediction & unlimited window: integer ~5-10, FP ~10-30. With realistic predictor (95-97%): integer drops to 4-6. Why processors stalled at 4-6 wide.
Compilers couldn't find static ILP for irregular code; memory latency variance broke schedules; code bloat; x86 emulation slow. OoO won. VLIW survives in DSPs and AI accelerators.
Determining if a load aliases an earlier store. LSQ tracks in-flight loads/stores in program order. Modern: store-set predictors learn which loads typically alias.
Hardware stack of return addresses pushed on CALL, popped on RET. ~16-32 entries deep. Mispredicts on tail calls, longjmp, RAS overflow.
Per-thread programming, but hardware groups 32 threads into a warp executing one instruction in lockstep across 32 lanes. Divergence halves performance.
Combines 32 thread loads into one transaction if they hit a single 128-byte line. Aligned contiguous = 1 transaction; random = up to 32. Critical for GPU performance.
Plots GFLOPS vs operational intensity (FLOPs/byte). Two ceilings: BW × intensity (sloped) and peak compute (flat). Diagnoses memory-bound vs compute-bound.
Hardware MMA: D = A × B + C, small matrix tile per instruction. Volta+. FP16/BF16/FP8/INT8. ~50× scalar SIMD throughput on GEMM workloads.
Registers → shared mem (~30 cyc) → L2 (~200 cyc) → HBM (~500 cyc, 3 TB/s). Shared mem is software-managed scratchpad — critical for tiling.
Wider SIMD draws more power per cycle. Sustained AVX-512 dropped clock 200-400 MHz on Skylake-X through Ice Lake. Sapphire Rapids reduced this.
Vector length implementation-defined; same binary runs on 128/512/2048-bit hardware. Loop predicates handle remainders cleanly.
Modified (only here, dirty), Exclusive (only here, clean → silent transition to M on write), Shared (multiple copies, clean), Invalid.
MOESI adds Owned: one cache supplies dirty data on snoops, eliminating writeback to memory. AMD Zen uses MOESI.
Snooping: O(N²) bandwidth, doesn't scale past ~16-32 cores. Directory: point-to-point messages, scales but adds latency + storage. Modern hyperscale = hybrid.
SC: program order preserved (slow). TSO (x86): allows store→load reorder. Weak (ARM, POWER): most reorders allowed; need DMB/DSB barriers.
Two cores write different bytes on same cache line → line bounces via coherence. Fix: pad with alignas(64) or per-thread structs. Apple uses 128-byte lines.
LL/SC (ARM/MIPS/RISC-V): two-instruction with reservation, can fail spuriously. CAS (x86): single atomic, susceptible to ABA. Modern ARM has both.
Each socket has local DRAM; remote access across fabric is slower. Local ~80ns, remote ~150-200ns. Software: numactl, thread pinning, NUMA-aware allocation.
Ring: O(N) latency, works to ~10 cores. Mesh: O(√N), used in 18+ core chips. Intel switched from ring to mesh on server SKX+.
Designed as one computer at the warehouse level: homogeneous HW, single owner, failure-tolerant SW, cost-driven. Why cloud is economical.
Map(k1,v1)→list((k2,v2)) then Reduce(k2,list(v2))→list(v3). Embarrassingly parallel, fault-tolerant, locality-aware. Foundation of WSC compute.
Power Usage Effectiveness = Total facility power / IT power. 1.0 = ideal, 2.0 = old enterprise, 1.1 = hyperscale. Free cooling + hot aisle containment + DC distribution.
Multi-stage non-blocking network with full bisection bandwidth. Spine-leaf is 2-tier flavor: leaf ↔ spine ↔ leaf, always 2 hops. Standard in WSCs.
Capex: servers 50-60%, networking 10-15%, power infra 10-15%, cooling 10%. Opex: power dominates. Server depreciation ≈ power over 5-yr lifecycle.
x86 (CISC) decodes to RISC-like micro-ops internally. ISA matters less than microarch + ecosystem. Apple/AWS proving ARM viable at the high end.
x86: base + index×scale + disp (most expressive, complex decode). ARM64: pre/post-indexed, register+ext register. MIPS: just register+offset.
Memory cheap now, code bloat doesn't matter. Decoder simplicity > encoding density. Cortex-M still uses Thumb for microcontrollers.
Direct-mapped (1 spot per address) → set-associative (n spots) → fully-associative (any spot). Modern: L1 = 4-8 way, L2/L3 = 8-16 way, TLB = fully assoc.
64 bytes (x86, ARM, MIPS standard) or 128 bytes (Apple M-series, NVIDIA L2). Larger = better spatial locality, worse false sharing.
On write miss, fetch block then write. Pairs with write-back. NT-stores (MOVNT, STNP) are escape hatch for streaming writes.
IF → ID → EX → MEM → WB. Hazards: structural (avoided by Harvard split), data (forwarding + 1-cycle load-use stall), control (predict / delay slot).
Before-i committed, at/after-i not visible. Required for page faults, debugging, virtual memory. ROB is the standard implementation.
Mispredict penalty scales with depth, power scales superlinearly with f, voltage stalled. Apple M1: 8-10 stages × 8-wide beats Intel 14+ stages × 4-wide.
MIPS R2000: instruction after branch always executes. Pre-OoO design. MIPS R6 deprecated; ARM and RISC-V never had it.
Routes EX/MEM and MEM/WB pipeline register outputs back to EX inputs to skip waiting for WB. Eliminates most RAW stalls in 5-stage.
Load result available end of MEM, dependent EX needs it earlier — 1 unavoidable stall. Compiler tries to schedule independent instruction in delay.
On miss, fetch the word the CPU is actually waiting for first; restart pipeline; rest of line streams in afterward. Reduces miss penalty.
Service hits while a miss is outstanding. Hit-under-miss → miss-under-miss. Essential for OoO cores; otherwise an L1 miss stalls all loads.
L1 predicts which way of a set holds the data; reads only that way. Gets near-direct-mapped hit time at set-associative miss rate.
Cache decoded micro-ops in execution order, bypassing decode for predicted paths. Pentium 4 used this; modern cores use micro-op cache instead (Sandy Bridge+).
HW: pattern detector (stride, stream). SW: compiler/programmer inserts PREFETCH/PRFM. SW handles irregular patterns; HW handles regular.
Hardware fetch-and-add, single instruction. ARMv8.1 added these to replace LL/SC loops; better contention behavior at scale.
Acquire: load + barrier preventing later ops from moving before. Release: barrier + store preventing earlier ops from moving after. Pairs to implement locks on weak models.
ARM's bus protocol: separate read/write channels, outstanding transactions, burst support, 5 channels (AR, R, AW, W, B). Standard for SoC IP integration.
Signals between async clock domains need synchronizers (2FF for single bits, async FIFO or handshake for buses). Metastability is the failure mode.
General matrix multiply: C = α·A·B + β·C. Compute-bound at large N (N³ ops, N² loads). Workhorse of DL training/inference; targeted by Tensor Cores, TPU MXU.
Stacked DRAM (3D-stacked dies + TSVs) with very wide interface. ~1 TB/s per stack on H100-class HBM3. Used in GPUs, AI accelerators, server CPUs.
Server should consume power proportional to utilization (e.g., 30% utilization → 30% power). Real servers historically draw 50%+ idle. WSC processors prioritize this.
